subject: Archaeology
title: The Titanic: Most Famous Wreck
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Titanic: Most Famous Wreck usable.

hook.text: The 'unsinkable' Titanic hit an iceberg on April 15, 1912, and sank in under three hours, killing 1,517 people.

buildup.text: The wreck lay undiscovered at 12,500 feet for 73 years. Robert Ballard found it in 1985 using deep-sea cameras.

discovery.text: The ship broke in two on the way down. The bow section is embedded 60 feet into the mud. The stern is shattered.

twist.text: Iron-eating bacteria are consuming the hull. Scientists estimate the wreck will be completely gone by 2030.

climax.text: In 2023, a submersible visiting the wreck imploded, killing five passengers. The Titanic still claims lives.

punchline.text: The Titanic is disappearing. Bacteria are finishing what the iceberg started.

quiz.question: What is happening to the Titanic wreck?
options: Treasure hunters are dismantling it piece by piece
Iron-eating bacteria are consuming the hull and may destroy it by 2030
Deep ocean currents are burying it deeper into the seabed
